summary:
Checker of the lane "css". All files of this check are in /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/perf/css/check/ (scripts, results/, logs/). Skill loaded: ariakit-general-workflow (the remote is github.com/ariakit/visonaut; no installed skill is specific to this repository). The repository was not written (`git status --short` is the same as at the start). The shared server on port 4320 got 2 light requests and 1 passive socket (no page load, no trace). My servers (4335 preview, 4336 and 4337 development) are stopped; no process listens on 4331 to 4339; port 4320 still has its listener.

The machine was much busier than during the research: the 1-minute load average was 51 to 659. So each time below is a comparison inside one interleaved run, with the CPU of the page slowed 4 times where it says so.

What I reproduced (counted, exact or within 1%): the sheet sizes and rule counts of the lab and of the real app; 0 duplicate rules in the lab and 581 in the build of the real app; the share of the recipes; the cost of one Button; the 44,747 B from apps/lab/audit and apps/lab/docs; the full reload after a document write and its removal with `source("./")`; the `css-update` to each of 11 documents; the stale sheet of the shared server (614,316 B against 517,151 B); the parse time of about 13 ms; the class weight of the HTML.

What I did not reproduce: the ratio 1.34 for "full sheet against page sheet" on the history page. I got 0.97 and 1.05 there, and 1.24 and 1.42 on the inbox page. The effect of the unused rules is not stable.

What the report did not measure, and I did (measured, production preview, CPU slowed 4 times, 5 runs of each, interleaved):
1. An empty style sheet. Style recalculation goes from 751 ms to 21 ms on the history page, and all main thread tasks go from 1,521 ms to 543 ms. So the CSS is 53% to 67% of the main thread time of one page. The cause is the rules that the page uses, not the size of the file.
2. One mechanism removed at a time. Without the `@property` rules, style recalculation goes down 60% to 69%. Without only the 51 typed `@property` rules of @ariakit/tailwind, it goes down 56% to 58%. Without the selectors with `:has()`: no change. Without the size containers: no change. Without the 225 style queries: 11% to 32% down. So the main cost has an exact place: the layer, text, and frame pipeline of @ariakit/tailwind that runs through its typed registered properties.
3. The gallery without its 10 preview frames: main thread tasks 818 ms against 3,792 ms. The frames are 78% of the gallery.
4. Development, one bare preview, no throttle: with an empty sheet the main thread time goes from 553 ms to 364 ms, but the last request ends at the same time (2.3 s against 2.5 s), and 287 of 289 requests and 18.3 of 18.9 MB stay. So in development the wall time is the development server, not the CSS.
5. A passive listener on the socket of the shared server for 7 minutes: 0 reload messages, because no lab file changed in that time. The reloads from document writes are real but not frequent now.
verdict:
The report is mostly right, and its counts are reliable. Four parts need a correction before the maintainer reads it.

1. Right: the CSS is large because of the primitives (73% to 76% of the bytes), and the lab adds 10% with the scan of its documents. The size of the file is not what costs time. The one-line fix `@import "tailwindcss" source("./");` works and breaks nothing that I could find.

2. Too weak: the report says that the per-element style cost is "a question for the runtime lane". I measured it. The CSS work is 53% to 67% of the main thread time of a page, and 56% to 69% of the style recalculation goes away when the registered properties (`@property`) are removed. So the answer to "is the problem our ariakit-ui primitives?" is yes, and the place is exact: the typed `@property` rules in @ariakit/tailwind/src/output.css (lines 1547 to 2251) and the formulas that write them. `:has()` and the size containers, which the report names as suspects, cost nothing in this test.

3. Not a fact: the ratios 1.34 and 1.10 (full sheet against page sheet). My runs gave 0.97 to 1.42 with ranges that overlap. Say "no stable effect".

4. Wrong for the real app: the proposed `@source not` lines. apps/web has no tabs.ts and no choice.ts, and its page src/routes/index.tsx uses table.ts. Also, the three "things for Ariakit" in the report have no time measurement behind them.

5. Overstated: "each document write reloads every page" is true, but the evidence for how often it happens is thin (at least 19 different minutes in 24 hours; 3 writes in the last 90 minutes; 0 in 7 minutes of listening). It is an occasional interruption, not a steady slowness.

corrections.claim: A sheet with only the classes of the page makes style recalculation 1.34 times faster on the history page and 1.10 times faster on the inbox page.
corrections.problem: Not reproduced (measured, same method, CPU slowed 4 times, 5 runs of each, interleaved). History: 771 ms with the page sheet against 751 ms with the full sheet (ratio 0.97, load 102 to 187), and 913 ms against 961 ms in the first session (ratio 1.05, load 64 to 74). Inbox: 206 ms against 293 ms (ratio 1.42, load 240 to 597), and 279 ms against 345 ms (ratio 1.24). The ranges overlap in three of the four runs. The research ranges also overlap (773 to 1,976 against 631 to 977).
corrections.fix: Write: "The unused rules have no stable effect on style recalculation: 0.97 to 1.42 times in four sessions, with ranges that overlap." Keep the conclusion (the file size is a small part). Remove the numbers 1.34 and 1.10 as facts.

corrections.claim: "Style recalculation, total" 1,002 ms and "Layout, total" 1,860 ms are given as two different costs.
corrections.problem: The research number for style is the counter RecalcStyleDuration of Performance.getMetrics. The trace event UpdateLayoutTree is only 16 to 33 ms on one page, and the trace event Layout is 864 to 961 ms. The reason (measured): the shell is a size container (`container: shell / inline-size`, 8 such elements on the history page), so Chrome does the style work of the whole page inside Layout. When I removed the 9 `container` declarations, the time moved: Layout 160 ms, UpdateLayoutTree 1,017 ms. So the trace sum "Layout" contains the style time.
corrections.fix: Name the metric in each table. Do not add "style" and "layout" from the two sources. The layout work itself is small: LayoutDuration is 132 to 151 ms on the history page.

corrections.claim: Cause 6: the style cost of each primitive element comes from many classes, custom properties, relative colors, 225 style queries, 423 selectors with :has(), and 247 registered properties. The exact cost of each mechanism is a question for the runtime lane.
corrections.problem: The list mixes mechanisms that cost time with mechanisms that do not. Measured (style recalculation, CPU slowed 4 times; history then inbox): no `:has()` selectors 769 ms and 267 ms against 751 ms and 293 ms (no change). No size containers: no gain. No style queries: 667 ms and 199 ms (11% and 32% down). No `@property` rules: 256 ms and 108 ms (66% and 63% down). Only the 51 typed `@property` rules of @ariakit/tailwind removed: 313 ms against 752 ms, and 125 ms against 287 ms (58% and 56% down). The 30 of ui.css: 21% and 24% down. The 78 of Tailwind: 8% and 11% down.
corrections.fix: Replace the list by the measured result. Name the place: the `@property` rules with `syntax: "<number>"`, `"<color>"`, or `"<length>"` in @ariakit/tailwind/src/output.css, lines 1547 to 2251 (for example `--_ak-lib`, `--_ak-li`, `--ak-layer`, `--ak-text`, `--_ak-frame-radius`), and the utilities that write them (`ak-layer*`, `ak-text`, `ak-ink-*`, `ak-frame*`). Say that the removal breaks the colors, so the number is an upper limit of a gain, not a fix.

corrections.claim: For Ariakit, the three things that would lower the cost for every app are (a) recipes whose unused variants do not reach the sheet, (b) ak-* value utilities that set only an input variable, (c) fewer classes for each element.
corrections.problem: None of the three has a time measurement. (a) and (b) lower the raw bytes only, and the bytes have no stable effect on time. (b): the formula `--ak-text: oklch(from var(--ak-layer) ...)` is in the sheet 38 times (counted, confirmed), but repeated text compresses: the sheet is 43 to 45 KB with brotli. (c) was not tested by any lane.
corrections.fix: Put the measured lever first: fewer typed registered properties that Chrome must compute for each element, or cheaper formulas in them. Keep (a) and (b) as size items with low priority. Mark (c) as not measured.

corrections.claim: The real app should add `@source not "./components/ariakit/styles/tabs.ts"`, `table.ts`, and `choice.ts`. In the lab, only the route /primitives uses these recipes.
corrections.problem: apps/web/src/components/ariakit/styles has 16 recipe files (counted). tabs.ts, choice.ts, checkbox.ts, and radio.ts are not there. table.ts is there and apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx imports Table: the line `@source not ".../table.ts"` removes 16,110 B that this page needs (counted: 332,367 B to 316,257 B). In the lab, the chrome also uses the five recipes: src/lab/ui/decision-panel.tsx (Radio), src/routes/pages.$surface.tsx (Tabs), src/routes/feedback.tsx, dev.fixtures.tsx, dev.hooks.tsx (Table), and src/explorations/components/status-mark/parts/context.tsx (Table). The directive itself works: in a copy of the lab it removed 83,234 B (counted).
corrections.fix: For the real app: copy only the primitive files that the design uses, as apps/web does today. Then no `@source not` line is necessary and nothing can go stale. Do not expect a speed gain from it: it lowers bytes only.

corrections.claim: Two findings in this path are large. (1) Each write to apps/lab/audit or apps/lab/docs reloads every open page: 2,652 to 3,179 requests on the gallery. Assumption: the reloads are a main part of what the maintainer saw.
corrections.problem: The mechanism is right and reproduced: `full-reload` in 4 of 4 writes on one preview (291 requests each), 10 to 11 `full-reload` messages on the gallery in 2 of 2 writes, and 0 messages in 4 of 4 writes with `source("./")`. But the frequency does not support "main part". The research count is at least 19 different minutes with a write in 24 hours. My count: 3 writes outside src in the last 90 minutes (04:28 README.md, 04:29 and 04:49 docs/design). A passive listener on the socket of the shared server got 0 messages in 420 s (05:12 to 05:19); no lab file changed in that time. The request count depends on the load: I got 213 to 237 requests in 6 s at a load of 250 to 320.
corrections.fix: Call it an occasional interruption: each write of an agent to a document reloads every open lab document one time. Keep the one-line fix. Add that apps/lab/README.md does the same (measured: 1 of 1). Use the count of `full-reload` messages, not the count of requests.

corrections.claim: The second half of the belief is mostly wrong: the size of the CSS file is not what makes the lab slow.
corrections.problem: True for the size, but the sentence hides the larger fact. The report did not test a page with no CSS. Measured: with an empty sheet, the main thread work of one page goes down 53% to 67% in the production form (history 1,521 ms to 543 ms; inbox 816 ms to 384 ms) and 34% in development (553 ms to 364 ms, no throttle). So CSS work is the largest part of the main thread time.
corrections.fix: Say both: "The file size is not the cause. The CSS is still the largest main thread cost, because of what the used rules compute for each element."

corrections.claim: The recipes are 355,565 B = 76% because `cv({ extend: [...] })` pulls whole recipes: Button reaches 11 recipe files.
corrections.problem: The number is right (my count with the real directive `@source not "./components/ariakit/styles"`: 337,784 B, 73% of the built sheet; Button alone: 14 files, 11 recipe files, +119,608 B). The mechanism is not `extend`. The bytes are in the sheet because Tailwind scans each file of the copied folder as text, used or not. `extend` only says which files an app must keep when it copies less.
corrections.fix: Write the mechanism as: "Tailwind scans src/components/ariakit/styles/*.ts as text. Each file that is in the folder costs all its classes." The app-side lever is the set of files that it copies.

corrections.claim: The primitives are about 277,000 of the 332,367 B of the real app today.
corrections.problem: Right only for the whole folder apps/web/src/components/ariakit (counted: 275,037 B of classes; the app without the folder is 65,985 B). The files styles/*.ts alone account for 120,005 B by removal, because the older component files of apps/web hold class strings themselves (for example layer.ariakit.react.tsx).
corrections.fix: Say "the folder components/ariakit" in place of "the recipes" for apps/web.

corrections.claim: The plugin freshStyles is necessary for a new file and costs nothing that can be measured.
corrections.problem: I did not run this again (no server without the plugin in this check). The source agrees: the plugin only calls `moduleGraph.invalidateModule` for src/styles.css, and @tailwindcss/vite registers only the files that it scanned before.
corrections.fix: Keep the claim, with the label "measured by the research lane only".

causes.cause: The style work that the primitive rules give the browser for each element. The layer, text, and frame pipeline of @ariakit/tailwind runs through typed registered properties. Chrome computes them (`oklch(from ...)`, `calc()`, `clamp()`) for each element that the utilities touch.
causes.size: Measured (production preview, CPU slowed 4 times, 5 runs of each, interleaved). Empty sheet: style recalculation 751 ms to 21 ms (history, 1,116 elements) and 293 ms to 4 ms (inbox, 300 elements); main thread tasks 1,521 to 543 ms and 816 to 384 ms. So CSS work is 53% to 67% of a page. Without the 51 typed `@property` rules of @ariakit/tailwind: 752 to 313 ms and 287 to 125 ms (58% and 56% down). Without all 247 `@property` rules: 60% to 69% down. Without the 30 of ui.css: 21% to 24% down. `:has()` selectors and size containers: no change. Style queries: 11% to 32% down. About 0.7 ms for each element with the CPU slowed 4 times; 143 to 149 ms for the 1,116 elements with no throttle (development).
causes.owner: primitives: @ariakit/tailwind (src/output.css, `@property` rules at lines 1547 to 2251 with syntax number, color, or length, and the utilities ak-layer*, ak-text, ak-ink-*, ak-frame* that write them); ui.css for a smaller part (30 `@property` rules)
causes.fix: No app-side fix except fewer elements (paging or a window for long lists). In @ariakit/tailwind: fewer typed registered properties for each element, or cheaper formulas. The removal test breaks the colors, so it shows the place and an upper limit, not the gain of a real change.
causes.sharedWithRealApp: Yes. This is the cost that goes to the real app with the design.

causes.cause: The lab shows live preview frames. The gallery has 11 documents. Each frame is a full page with its own copy of the sheet and its own style work.
causes.size: Measured (production preview, CPU slowed 4 times, 5 runs, load 76 to 119): main thread tasks 3,792 ms with the 10 frames and 818 ms when each frame gets an empty document (78% less). Parse of the sheet: 129 ms for 11 documents against 12.5 ms for 1.
causes.fix: Fewer live frames on one lab page: pictures, or frames that load when the user opens them.
causes.sharedWithRealApp: No. The real app has 1 document.

causes.cause: The development server sends a page as many unbundled modules. This is the wall time of a page in development.
causes.size: Measured (development copy, one bare preview, no throttle, load 453 to 534): 289 requests and 18.9 MB. With an empty sheet: 287 requests and 18.3 MB, and the last request ends at 2,465 ms against 2,336 ms (no gain). The main thread work is 553 ms with the sheet and 364 ms without it. The sheet is 517,832 B of the 18.9 MB (2.7%).
causes.owner: tool stack (Vite development mode with the Cloudflare plugin and TanStack Start); the details belong to the development server lane

causes.cause: Tailwind scans the whole Vite root of the lab: apps/lab/audit, apps/lab/docs, and apps/lab/README.md. The hook hotUpdate of @tailwindcss/vite sends `full-reload` when a scanned file that is not a module changes.
causes.size: Measured: `full-reload` in 4 of 4 writes on one preview (291 requests each), 10 to 11 `full-reload` messages on the gallery in 2 of 2 writes, also for README.md and audit/content/findings.json (1 of 1 each). With `source("./")`: 0 messages in 4 of 4 writes. Counted: +44,747 B of CSS (465,819 to 421,072 B); 767 scanned files against 290; Tailwind generation 58 ms against 34 ms (median). Frequency: low. At least 19 different minutes with a write in 24 hours (research count); 3 writes in the last 90 minutes; 0 messages in 420 s of listening on the shared server.
causes.owner: lab (configuration and the place of its documents); the mechanism is in @tailwindcss/vite
causes.fix: One line in apps/lab/src/styles.css: `@import "tailwindcss" source("./");`. Checked: no file of src imports from audit or docs, and the audit page has its own inline style, so nothing breaks.
causes.sharedWithRealApp: Partly. apps/web scans 78 files outside src (migrations 33, tooling 39, CHANGELOG.md, and 5 others). They add 0 B (counted). The reload there follows from the plugin source and was not tested. Those files change rarely.

causes.cause: Each edit of a scanned source file makes Vite send `css-update /src/styles.css?direct` to each open document. Each document fetches and applies the whole sheet again.
causes.size: Measured. One preview: 1 message, 1 request of 517,217 B, style recalculation 38 to 63 ms, tasks 92 to 209 ms (no throttle, load 104 to 119). Gallery: 10 to 11 messages and 10 to 11 sheet requests for one edit; style recalculation 1,001 to 1,735 ms in 6 s (the control was not clean at a load of 250 to 320: 372 to 737 ms).
causes.owner: tool stack (Vite and @tailwindcss/vite), multiplied by the frames of the lab and by the per-element style cost
causes.fix: None in one line. Fewer live frames lowers it in the lab.
causes.sharedWithRealApp: Yes for the mechanism (about 40 to 60 ms for one document). No for the factor 11.

causes.cause: The development sheet of a long session only grows: @tailwindcss/vite keeps `candidates = new Set` and only adds to it.
causes.size: Counted at 05:20: shared server 614,316 B and 3,884 rules; the current source gives 517,151 B and 2,713 rules. 1,171 rules (88,556 B) are only in the shared sheet; 1,088 of them are for classes that are in no file now; 0 rules are only in the new sheet. Effect on time: small, because unused rules have no stable effect.
causes.owner: tool stack, made visible by a server that is never restarted
causes.fix: Restart the development server after a large removal of files.
causes.sharedWithRealApp: Yes, in a long development session. Not in a build.

causes.cause: The size of the style sheet itself (parse, and rules that the page does not use).
causes.size: Counted: lab 474,725 B built (66,264 gzip, 45,506 brotli, 3,022 rules, 0 duplicate rules); recipes 73% to 76%, lab documents 10%, lab classes 7%. Measured: parse 12.9 and 13.1 ms for one document (CPU slowed 4 times). Full sheet against page sheet: 0.97 to 1.42 times, not stable.
causes.owner: primitives for the bytes; as a cause of slowness: small
causes.fix: Scan src only (-44,747 B). Copy only the primitive files that the app uses. Expect smaller files, not a faster page.
causes.sharedWithRealApp: Yes for the size. The real app has 332,367 B of different rules, and its build has 464,666 B because 581 rules (114,948 B) are in it two times (counted, confirmed).

causes.cause: The ak-* utilities repeat their formulas in each class and in each variant (for example `@utility ak-ink-*`, src/output.css line 816).
causes.size: Counted: `--ak-text: oklch(from var(--ak-layer) ...)` is in the sheet 38 times (confirmed). The research count of 72,313 B of repeated blocks was not run again. No time effect is measured, and the repeated text compresses.
causes.fix: Low priority. A split into one formula class and one value class lowers raw bytes only.

causes.size: Not run again. Research: necessary for a new file (7 of 7 rounds), no cost that can be measured. The source agrees: it only drops the cache entry of src/styles.css.
causes.owner: lab; not a cause of the slowness

causes.size: Measured: 1-minute load average 51 to 659 during this check (14 to 88 during the research). The document of a development page needed 191 to 690 ms for its first byte at these loads.
causes.fix: None in the code. Measure again on a quiet machine before a decision that depends on an absolute time.

remainingDoubts: Every time in this check was measured at a 1-minute load average of 51 to 659. The ratios inside one interleaved run are usable. No millisecond value is the speed of the app on a quiet machine.

The `@property` test removes rules that the design needs: without them the layer colors and the frames are gone (pictures: results/shot.history.full.png and results/shot.history.no-property.png). So 56% to 69% is the cost of the whole pipeline that these registrations make possible, and an upper limit for a gain. I did not measure which of the 51 properties cost the most, or what a real change in @ariakit/tailwind would save.
The effect of the unused rules is not settled: 0.97 to 1.42 in four sessions. A quiet machine and more runs are necessary to say if it is 0% or about 20%.

The gallery in development was not measured in a reliable way. At a load of about 550 the 10 frames did not finish in the 4 s window (1,382 requests of about 3,188). The number 78% for the frames is from the production preview.
I do not know what the maintainer had open, at which time, and at which machine load. The share of each cause in what he saw is an assumption. The machine load can be a large part of it.
How often document writes happened while the maintainer used the lab is unknown. The modification times give only a lower limit (a file that was written 10 times counts one time).

Not run again in this check: the coverage numbers (8% to 24% of the rules for a page), the estimate of the sheet of the real app with the new design, the count of 72,313 B of repeated blocks, the regeneration timing with and without freshStyles, and the test that freshStyles is necessary.
apps/web was not run in a browser. Its numbers are from its source and its existing build. The reload after a change of CHANGELOG.md or a migration was not tested there.
The cost of the count of classes for each element (19 for a Text, up to 65 for a glider) was not tested by any lane.
Only Chrome ran. Safari and Firefox compute registered properties and style queries in their own way.
The fixed source is the lab of 04:27 (round 3 in progress), not the round 2 state that the maintainer used. The current source gives the same sheet size (465,819 B minified in my pipeline for both).
